records.note: Personal statement about the author's daughter and a stuffed toy. Not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or adoption outcome. 'Won't be bullied' names no event that a third party decides.
Statement about the author's own writing skill ('my peak is less good than it will be tomorrow'). Not one of the five areas, and only the author's own practice decides it.
Speculation about personal trouble from his own satire ('might get me in trouble'). No company, case, body or event is named; the subject (the author's personal exposure) is outside the five areas.

The author adopts Dave Chase's forecast ('I can see the writing on the wall'), so THIRD_PARTY does not apply, but 'the coming apocalypse in liability for corporate America' is a slogan: no case, court, ruling, settlement or threshold can be written without inventing the outcome type. 'Coming' is not a deadline. The Schlichter target list is Chase's report, not the author's claim.

Rhetorical alternative offered to an unnamed 'you' (corporate decision-makers): 'class action lawyers and federal regulators dismantle the next decade of your fortune'. A metaphor with no plaintiff, agency, case, company or threshold; 'the next decade' attaches to the fortune, not to an event. Nothing can be written without inventing.

Statement of immediate personal intention ('I'm going to get back to it now') about the author's own paper. No publication, journal or date is asserted, and the subject is outside the five areas. Read as a publication commitment it would be CONTROL.

Restates The Joint Commission's announced 2024 sentinel-event policy ('has decided'). The deciding body had published the decision on the statement date; the sentence passes on information, not an expectation.

'A huge pain in the neck' and 'a big deal' name no observable event; 'more suicides' has no countable set or series (sentinel-event counts under the new rule have no baseline for 'more'). The fear clause about 'the numbers' has no threshold. Nothing can be written without inventing a metric.
'Brings an entire new level of seriousness to post-discharge suicide' names no observable event, benchmark or threshold; it is also present tense. Nothing can be written without inventing a metric.

'As sobering as I fear they will be' is an expectation about sentinel-event suicide counts with no threshold and no named series; 'sobering' is not a number. 'I hope they push us towards more effective treatments' states a preference, and 'more effective treatments' has no set. Nothing can be written.
Cohort-level risk statement about young people's social lives ('There is a risk of never having...'). Not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or adoption outcome; 'never' is not a deadline.
Announcement of the author's own conference (RAMHT, listed in his affiliations as organizer) on 7 January 2024. His organization makes it happen: commitment, not forecast.

Present-tense description of Compass Pathways' business ('is the biotech company bringing ... Comp360, to market'), read like 'is now being brought to market' in an earlier packet. No approval, launch or date is asserted; an FDA approval event would be the coder's inference, not the author's call.

'Still a lot of research to be done before these become well-established medicines' has no benchmark for 'well-established', no countable set ('these') and no date. The closing 'I am hopeful' sentence is coded at owen-0822.

'I look forward to the kinds of risk mitigation measures needed' states a wish, as with 'I look forward to the replication' in an earlier packet. No regulator, decision, drug approval or REMS requirement is asserted; 'needed' reads as normative.

'I am hopeful we will have' states a preference, as with 'my hope' in an earlier packet. Even read as a call, 'new and powerful treatments for depression' names no asset or decision (COMP360 appears only in context), and 'in the near future' is not a deadline.

Interpretation of the published phase 2b result ('It's a hint that the drug is much more powerful than we suspected'; 'phase 3 differences in phase 2 size trials'). No phase 3 trial, endpoint, effect-size threshold or date is asserted; 'more powerful' is a comparative without a benchmark. The finder's 'likely' is not in the quote, and the finder's hint cites events after the statement date; it is not used.

'I hope our hospitals can include SAINT' states a wish, not an expectation (contrast the flat assertion 'and soon, in hospital settings' admitted in an earlier packet). 'Our hospitals' has no set and 'very shortly' is not a deadline.
Announcement of the author's own conference (RAMHT) on 7 January 2024. Commitment, not forecast.
Editorial plan for the author's own newsletter ('This year? I am taking a crack ... for things that are not pharmaceuticals'). His publication decides; commitment, not forecast.

Logistics of the author's own event ('will be discussed at Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment 2024 this Sunday'). 'Already an FDA breakthrough' is information about the past. Commitment, not forecast.
Announcement of the author's own first in-person event (RAMHT 2024, 7 January 2024). Commitment, not forecast.

No adoption event, hospital count, series or date is asserted; 'changing brain medicine' is also a slogan. Present-tense fit claims about SAINT in inpatient settings were read the same way in earlier packets.

event.asset: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) devices, any manufacturer
event.title: FDA authorizes a TMS device for a new indication
event.proposition: The FDA grants a 510(k) clearance, De Novo authorization or PMA approval for a transcranial magnetic stimulation device for a disease or condition not already authorized for any TMS device at the statement date.
event.criterion: TRUE on the decision date in the FDA 510(k), De Novo or PMA database of a marketing authorization, dated after 2024-01-04, for a transcranial magnetic stimulation device whose indications-for-use statement names a disease or condition that no TMS device was authorized for on 2024-01-04. The four indications the forecaster lists (major depressive disorder including treatment-resistant depression, anxious depression, smoking cessation, obsessive-compulsive disorder) and migraine (single-pulse TMS, authorized before the statement date) do not count. A new patient population (for example an age range) or a new protocol within an already authorized condition, a breakthrough device designation, an investigational device exemption and an authorization outside the United States do not count. Resolution source: the FDA 510(k) Premarket Notification database, with the De Novo and PMA databases for the other pathways.

resolution_source.name: FDA 510(k) Premarket Notification database (De Novo and PMA databases for other pathways)

readings: 'indications' = FDA-authorized indications for use of TMS devices. The forecaster lists the four conditions he treats as current; they are the FDA-cleared psychiatric and addiction indications at the statement date.
'more indications' = at least one disease or condition new to TMS as a device class; one authorization for one new condition suffices. Any TMS manufacturer counts, since the forecaster names none.
A population expansion or a protocol change within an already authorized condition is not a new indication; a listed condition under another name (MDD for TRD) is not new.

records.deadline_text: with more indications on the way
records.stage_note: At the statement date TMS devices are FDA-cleared for the four conditions the forecaster lists (MDD including TRD, anxious depression, smoking cessation, OCD) and single-pulse TMS for migraine. The forecaster names no pending submission, so device_510k_clearance_after_submission does not fit, and no class covers a new indication for a device class: b is null.
records.note: Admitted: the FDA, not the forecaster's organizations, decides indications, and 'more indications' has a countable set because the forecaster lists the current four. The flat assertion 'on the way' carries no hedge and is read like the lexicon A phrase 'is coming': bin A, asserts true. 'On the way' is not a deadline, so the item is undated (24-month window from 2024-01-04). affiliated false: the event names the FDA and TMS devices of any manufacturer, and none of the forecaster's listed affiliations is a TMS device maker; he provides TMS at Radial, which the event does not name, so that interest is recorded here only. Reading logged: an indication is a disease or condition, not a population or protocol.

Clinical prognosis about individual patients (TMS benefits 'likely ... not permanent'; retreatment 'likely to be necessary'). No third party decides it, and it is not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or adoption outcome.
'It will change what you understand to be possible' is a rhetorical impact claim about a just-published paper. No observable event, benchmark or threshold can be written.

A Nobel Prize in Medicine for Nolan Williams is not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or adoption outcome. The sentence is also hyperbolic advocacy ('perhaps ... will do it') for the author's own declared campaign.
'Might be the kind of broad spectrum and potent healing we all hope for access to' names no approval, trial result, adoption event, payer decision or date. Hedged hope with nothing resolvable.
Speaker logistics for the author's own event (RAMHT 2024, 7 January 2024). Commitment, not forecast.

Umbrella statement over seven PTSD technologies the author sees as 'plausibly useful on the horizon'. No event, countable set, benchmark or date; the Lykos filing and the GammaCore request are stated as facts, not as approval calls.

'With more data coming' has no countable set: what counts as more data (a poster, a publication, a press release) is undefined, the sponsor is not named in the text, and 'coming' is not a deadline. Not a trial_result claim: no endpoint or direction is asserted.
Launch of PRISM at Fermata, the author's own practice and CRO ('we launch this treatment at Fermata'). Commitment, not forecast.

'More coming in GAD' has no trial, sponsor, countable set or threshold, and 'on the horizon' is not a deadline. The parenthetical ('pre-print from my group') points to the author's own group, so a specific reading would be CONTROL.
More real-life events of the author's own newsletter ('there will be more of these real-life newsletter events coming'). Commitment, not forecast.
A new RAMHT section in the author's own newsletter. Commitment, not forecast.

Personal statement about the author's future poetry contest entries ('knowing I will fail'). Outside the five areas.
